names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 7 Αυγούστου, «Όσια Ποταμία η Θαυματουργή», with the rank words and the epithets left off.

Name page 2650 of days.pravoslavie.ru is «Потамия, прмц.»; the rank is stripped, and the calendar gives no surname and no epithet. The day line gives the genitive «Потамии». `fk.mjs` on the stored string returns NONE.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 7 августа ст. ст. — «Прмц. Потамии чудотворицы (IV).»

attestations.note: The day's seventh entry and the same menologion day as the folder's Greek row, which is its only other venerated one. «Прмц.» is the `venerable-martyr` and «чудотворицы» the `wonderworker` the folder's `types` already carry. NO `dates` WERE WRITTEN: the line's «(IV)» is the fourth century and would be this folder's first date of any kind, and this wave has declined to write a first date off a bare Roman numeral on a line — the standing author question. The reading life4394 was not opened. The day page prints no hymn under her name.
Not checked: doxologia.ro's calendar for the same civil day (1 October 2026).

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 7ης Αυγούστου — «Όσια Ποταμία η Θαυματουργή»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 7 Αυγούστου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. The whole of the entry is one sentence, «Η Όσια Ποταμία η Θαυματουργή μαρτύρησε δια ξίφους», with a couplet above it that plays on her name: slain by the sword for Christ, Potamia pours out rivers of wonders. There is no year, no place and no judge, so there is no `dates` object and no `locations` object. She is not the corpus's `potamiaena`, whom the sources keep elsewhere. The listing calls her Όσια and the sentence says she was martyred, so `types` carries both readings. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence on the life page, which was grepped for there and not on the listing. The page prints no apolytikion and no kontakion, so this folder takes no hymn.
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue on pravoslavno.rs for the corresponding Julian day (1 October 2026).
